title: Alphabet Stock: Buy or Sell? (My Final Verdict)
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; note: captions garbled in places
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA reviews Alphabet after the stock fell a further 10% post-earnings, extending a slide from about $400. Revenue rose 25%, R&D rose 36% on AI talent and depreciation, and operating profit still grew 30%. The disappointment is an $8.2 billion quarterly loss on the SpaceX holding — he wishes Alphabet had sold the stake after the IPO pop and would like it to sell what it can. Encouragingly, flat operating cash flow partly reflects a TPU inventory build-up, with TPU demand insatiable. The balance sheet is strong: over $265 billion of cash against $125 billion of long-term debt. Google Cloud grew revenue by over 100% with a $561 billion backlog, about 55% of which (roughly $280 billion) should convert to revenue over the next 24 months. Capex of $200 billion is guided for 2026 and is set to rise significantly in 2027 — he guesses $250–300 billion. Return on invested capital has been above 30% since 2025 (38% most recently) against a 9.8% weighted average cost of capital, so he trusts management to earn an attractive return on the spend. His DCF fair-value figure was garbled in the auto-captions and could not be read, so it is not recorded; at $279 and a forward P/E of 18.6 the stock looks undervalued on both methods. He calls it a buying opportunity with high conviction. Call: GOOGL BUY (reiterated; prior BUY 31 October).
